title: Improve cost of container commit
body:
The recent security fixes, in addition to the core write escapes, also switched to use `*os.Root` for creating tar archives. Because `*os.Root` resolves deeply nested paths one directory at a time, that is more costly, particularly with FUSE. Improve some of that performance again.

- Move the `stat` and xattr abstractions from `pkg/system` to `internal/…`. We just added public `stat.RootL…` and they are now unused, so let’s not make that mistake again.
- Avoid some wholly redundant `root.Lstat` calls when the data is already provided by fs.WalkDir()`
- When using `*os.Root`, instead using a single root at the top level (paying the cost of the directory walk on each operation), create also a per-directory `parentRoot` and do all operations only on base names. The current plan in Go is to replace the directory walk with a single `openat2` syscall, but they would still do a separate syscall for the actual operation; so, using a `parentRoot`, we can eliminate (currently) the directory walk and (in the future) the `openat2`.
- Because most of our operations don’t control the walk directly and obtain individual path names, introduce `internal/rootlookupcache`, so that consecutive operations on files in the same directory don’t need to open the directory repeatedly.
- For the Linux `Changes…` operation, where we are doing the directory walk manually, also use the cache and use basename-only operations.
- Operations on xattrs need an `O_PATH` or similar handle of the individual file. Instead of creating that for each syscall, manage the lifetime explicitly as an `xattr.Handle`.

This is not ideal, but to do better we’d need to wholly replace `fs.WalkDir`, with something more complex (e.g. keeping the last 10 or so parent handles). That can still be done in the future; and if it eliminates the need of `rootlookupcache`, we can just drop it again.

Mostly mitigates https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29833 , see there for some numbers.
